alignments.note: The ASV recasts this one nominal with its construct dependent as a head noun plus a relative clause of making; the supplied antecedent, relative and verb belong to that noun's unit and head on the English verb the recasting writes (rules 46, 43). The marginal literal gloss 'A man of friends' corroborates the reading without deciding it (rule 38).
Dependent noun keeps its own English; the supplied quantifying determiner joins its unit and is never the head (rule 15).

Supplied lexical verb together with the object supplied alongside it: the Hebrew clause writes neither, so no morpheme licenses either word and they are one added unit (rules 20, 2). Italics corroborate without deciding (rule 7).
Written preposition before the infinitive, which the ASV recasts as a noun (rule 52).

Supplied possessive with no suffix or other possessive morpheme in the clause (rule 18's closing sentence); a separate added unit from 'doeth it' because the preposition's own rendering stands between them (rule 2).
Infinitive recast as a verbal noun (rule 52).
Positive existential particle takes the presentative frame the ASV writes for it, headed on the finite word (rules 21, 50).
Anarthrous substantival participle with its indefinite article (rules 46, 15). The marginal literal gloss 'lover' is read and set aside (rule 38).
Articleless attributive recast as a relative clause keeps the supplied relative with the attributive itself (rule 41).
Comparative preposition with the degree word the ASV writes beside it; the unit heads on 'than' (rule 24). Keeping 'closer' with the attributive participle was the competing reading (rule 8).

review_notes: 'doeth it' and 'his own' are two added runs rather than one, since the rendered preposition 'to' stands between them (rule 2).
